contents.name: §1 n°1-2: analytic subsets of C^n (local zero loci of holomorphic functions) and the notion of analytic space
§1 n°3-4: the local rings of an analytic space and their relation to the rings of germs of holomorphic functions

Lemme 1 (§1 n°5): the Zariski topology is coarser than the usual topology of C^n, Zariski-locally closed subsets are analytic, regular maps are holomorphic, and bi-regular isomorphisms are analytic isomorphisms

Proposition 2 (§2 n°5, printed pp. 8-9): every complex algebraic variety carries a unique analytic structure for which every algebraic chart is an analytic chart; the analytification X^an is separated and countable at infinity
Corollaire 3 (§2 n°6, printed p. 11): an irreducible algebraic variety of dimension r has analytification of analytic dimension r at every point
Proposition 6 (§2 n°7, printed p. 12): an algebraic variety is complete if and only if its analytification is compact
